answer: Randomness-anchored join lottery. Each period a public verifiable random beacon selects a small subset of pending agents; only those may register, and every selection consumes a fresh cedar-seeded slot the attacker cannot predict before the beacon fires. Because identities must be pre-created and held through unknown waiting times, the attacker pays continuous idle-agent upkeep plus a widening spiral of missed slots, making mass registration cost scale with time rather than a flat fee.
